liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Might Quinn** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls the Quinn encore great; The Dylan cover Quinn in this show delivers for the reviewer [14][17]
- **Touch Of Grey** (1 review): Opener meant to lift spirits after the previous night's ending, though the reviewer finds it not that grand [8]
- **Little Red Rooster** (1 review): Reviewer hears Bobby's playing as sharp, with some hounds howling in the crowd [8]
- **Row Jimmy** (1 review): Reviewer finds Row Jimmy sweet [18]
- **Far From Me** (1 review): Brent's eager playing lifts the song [8]
- **Box Of Rain** (1 review): Reviewer finds Box Of Rain solid [18]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Bobby's Looks Like Rain has stuck in the reviewer's memory for years [7]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review): Reviewer recalls Jerry playing a ripping Terrapin [7]

## The recordings

- **gd88-04-24.sbd.hinko.31976.sbeok.flacf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 141 min; rated 3.83/5 by 6 [1]. Said about its sound: Vocals sit up front in the mix on this matrix; Sound quality is excellent, with Jerry's vocals coming through clearly [9][17]
- **gd1988-04-24.152579.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 142 min [2]
- **gd1988-04-24.152480.ultramatrix.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 19 songs; 142 min [3]
- **gd88-04-24.aud-fob.leeds.16887.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 141 min; rated 4.5/5 by 12 [4]. Said about its sound: Recording is notably spacious and high quality; Reviewer prefers this audience recording over the soundboard, crediting Albix and the Laptaper duo [12][18]

## Around the show

- First set begins slow and mellow before building; Jerry sounds a bit worn at the start [9]
- Reviewer attended; a stranger supplied party favors, a hotel room and fourth-row seats, with substances shared around [10]
- Reviewer attended this final night of a three-night Irvine Meadows run; the crowd shouted for Phil [14]
- Reviewer remembers Bobby playing spot-on throughout the whole Irvine run [7]
- Reviewer calls it a typical, steady show of the era, with strong playing, nothing exceptional and no flops [10]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd88-04-24.sbd.hinko.31976.sbeok.flacf**: transferred by Darryl Hinko; source: Soundboard patched with Audience [1]. Also: Source is a front-of-board audience recording, taken through PCM, DAT and CDR, then converted to SHN; Audience patch covers the stretch after Masterpiece; the uploader admits exact patch boundaries are unknown [1]
- **gd1988-04-24.152579.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  May 18, 2021; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG) [2]. Also: Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; Paul B. and Steven Leeds supplied the patch source; This version is a 24-bit to 16-bit conversion at 44.1 kHz of another release [2]
- **gd1988-04-24.152480.ultramatrix.miller.flac2496**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  May 18, 2021; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG) [3]. Also: Recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; Paul B. and Steven Leeds supplied the patch source [3]
- **gd88-04-24.aud-fob.leeds.16887.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience: Unknown Mics [4]. Also: Taper announces the date and his mic setup at the start: 110-degree ORTF; Front-of-board audience recording, via PCM, DAT and CDR, converted to seekable SHN; Steven Leeds converted it and seeded it to etree, with help from Paul B [4][12]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1988-04-24 Grateful Dead Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1988-04-24-grateful-dead-backstage-pass/) [20]
